title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Followup
summary: Follow-up on Friday's 5xx/timeouts incident during POC load run. Reviewed root causes (rate limiting, proxy timeouts, retry configs), temporary mitigations, and next steps: Redwood to provide tuned retry/backoff + timeout recommendations and a short patch for gateway timeouts; NexaCare to run extended load and share full traces.
next_steps: Redwood to send retry/backoff and timeout config recommendations + sample nginx/gateway patch by 2026-05-18
NexaCare to run 2-hour extended load (steady 300 rps) with tracing enabled and upload logs by 2026-05-20
Schedule follow-up focused on KV cache warmup and prefix cache strategy for 2026-05-22
Redwood SE to provision dedicated test pool for spike tests by 2026-05-19
action_items: Priya Desai - produce patch and config diff for gateway timeouts and exponential backoff - due 2026-05-18
Maya Singh - run extended 2-hour load test and upload traces/logs to shared drive - due 2026-05-20
Taylor Nguyen - enable token-level tracing on the POC cluster and share example traces - due 2026-05-19
Alex Kim - send updated engagement plan and pricing guardrail for dedicated capacity if chosen - due 2026-05-21
transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're here to follow up on the Friday run where you hit those 5xx spikes and timeouts. Aim is to go over what we saw, what we've changed, and next steps.
00:15 Jordan Lee: Thanks Alex. Appreciate the quick turnaround. Quick context — we were doing the 1hr steady 200 rps then a sudden ramp to 400 for 10 minutes and that's where we saw the errors.
00:33 Priya Desai: Right, so what we observed in the telemetry — and caveat, some of the names in the logs got munged — was increased queueing at the gateway (we saw 504s from the nginx/proxy) and a correlated rise in backend token generation latencies.
00:50 Maya Singh: Correct, we saw about 12% 5xxs during the spike window, mostly 504/502s. There were also a handful of 429s earlier.
01:05 Alex Kim: Two things to separate: the 429s are rate limiting at the edge — our API tier limit kicked in — and the 5xx/504s look like upstream timeouts where the gateway gave up waiting for the inference runtime.
01:20 Carlos Ruiz: Is that from the KV cash — K-V cash — like the cache warmup? I saw some logs referencing cache misses.
01:30 Priya Desai: Yeah, KV cache misses are part of it. When you ramp, the model needs to populate KV cache for longer context and that can raise per-request latency for the first few tokens. If you have a lot of cold starts combined with gateway timeouts and strict retry behavior, you get the error cascade.
01:48 Jordan Lee: So is the fix to raise timeouts at the gateway, or to change retry behavior? We don't want to mask real failures.
01:58 Taylor Nguyen: From the infra side, we recommended three immediate mitigations: bump gateway timeout from 30s to 60s for the POC route, add exponential backoff with jitter on client retries, and introduce a small warmup burst before full ramp to prefill the KV cache.
02:15 Ellen Park: For security and compliance, if you increase timeouts or enable retries, we need to ensure logs still capture full request IDs and traces, and that SRs to KMS are not re-sent in a way that duplicates billing.
02:30 Priya Desai: Good call. The request ID tracing is on by default in the POC cluster, but we will double-check that the gateway passes the X-Trace headers through.
02:45 Jordan Lee: What about autoscaling? We thought Redwood was autoscaling based on throughput. Why did we still hit capacity?
02:55 Priya Desai: Autoscaling is per pool and has a ramp duration. With a sudden 2x spike, the new pods or GPU slots might not be available in time — plus model load time matters. For this POC you're on a shared hosted pool with burst limits. If you need headroom, we can provision a small dedicated test pool to avoid shared contention.
03:15 Jordan Lee: Okay that's sensible. Cost increase for a dedicated pool might be acceptable for the pilot if it stabilizes SLOs. We'll need an estimate.
03:28 Alex Kim: We'll include a short delta estimate for a small dedicated pool in the follow-up.
03:35 Carlos Ruiz: There were also a couple of logs where 'Redwood-verified' model name got mungled and showed as 'Radwood-verified' in our trace exports — just FYI, the export mapping has some OCR-ish artifacts.
03:50 Priya Desai: Yep, transcription/labeling in the logs sometimes messes up names, we saw that too. Not functionally relevant but makes root cause analysis noisy.
04:05 Maya Singh: Regarding retries, our current client has 3 retries at fixed 2s intervals which basically floods the system during the spike. We want recommendation for backoff and max retries.
04:18 Priya Desai: Recommended pattern: client-side 2 retries with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g., 200ms then 800ms + jitter), and serverside short-circuit 429 handling with a small grace window. Also, keep the original request timeout slightly shorter than gateway so retries don't cause double load.
04:40 Jordan Lee: Can Redwood provide a sample nginx/gateway patch? We use Kong/nginx combo.
04:48 Alex Kim: Yes, Priya will produce a small diff for common proxies (nginx/Kong) that bumps proxy_read_timeout, proxy_connect_timeout, and includes header passthrough for X-Trace and X-Request-ID.
05:05 Ellen Park: We'll need to run that patch through our security review — specifically want notes on how it affects connection draining and session affinity.
05:18 Priya Desai: We'll annotate the patch with migration notes (drain strategy, sticky sessions) and call out any potential impact to connection counts.
05:30 Carlos Ruiz: On the model side, do we need to change quantization or batch sizes? We saw higher token latencies when requests had 2-3k tokens.
05:42 Taylor Nguyen: Large tokens definitely amplify KV cache build up. For the pilot, we suggested capping request size to 2048 tokens for heavy load windows and applying per-route batching size limits. Also we can recommend quantization profiles that reduce per-token compute. We'll include those recommendations in the doc.
06:00 Jordan Lee: Any security concerns with prefix caching? We operate under HIPAA-ish constraints and don't want cross-tenant leakage.
06:12 Priya Desai: Prefix/KV caching is always per-tenant in the POC setup; we don't share cache entries across customers. We will provide an architecture diagram for the cache isolation to Ellen so you can sign off.
06:30 Ellen Park: Please include mention of KMS usage for keys in the diagram. We require that for any private deployment.
06:40 Alex Kim: Noted.
06:45 Priya Desai: Quick note on the 429s: they likely came from client-side burst plus our shared pool rate limit. We're recommending two levers: client retry/backoff and optionally short-term quota bump for the load window.
07:00 Jordan Lee: If we bump quota for the POC, what are the guardrails? We don't want to pay a lot.
07:08 Alex Kim: We'll propose a small temporary bump with a spend cap and alerting. Also show delta cost for a dedicated tiny pool versus hosted bump.
07:22 Maya Singh: Can you also share the exact metric queries you used to identify that the 504s were gateway timeouts? Our ops people want to reproduce the dashboard.
07:30 Priya Desai: Yes — we'll share the PromQL and the dashboard JSON. We'll also add the sample trace span that shows proxy->runtime timeout.
07:42 Jordan Lee: Great. I flagged one more oddity: some of our retry logs show duplicate KMS calls which worried security. Could retries be re-sending key unwraps?
07:52 Taylor Nguyen: The SDK should be idempotent-aware for KMS operations. If not, we can wrap the KMS call with an idempotency token or ensure retries don't re-execute crypto operations. We'll double-check in our SDK integration notes and include a pattern.
08:10 Ellen Park: Perfect. Also can you confirm SOC2/ISO artifacts are still available? We may need them for procurement fast-track.
08:20 Alex Kim: Yes, we'll re-share the SOC2 Type II and ISO briefs and send an onboarding checklist for auditors.
08:28 Jordan Lee: Timeline question: if we make these changes and run the extended test, how quickly can we schedule a follow-up to validate?
08:36 Alex Kim: Assuming Priya's patch goes out by 5/18 and you run a 2-hour load by 5/20, we can meet the week of 5/22. We proposed May 22 for a KV cache warmup deep-dive.
08:48 Priya Desai: One more operational note — we're turning on slightly more verbose retry logs for a 24-hour window to catch flakey behaviors; we'll keep them restricted.
09:00 Jordan Lee: Ok thanks. Quick recap before we close?
09:05 Alex Kim: Recap: root cause is cascade from client burst + cold KV cache + gateway timeouts. Immediate mitigations: gateway timeout bump + client exponential backoff + small warmup before ramp. Medium term: consider dedicated test pool and cap request sizes during high-throughput tests. Action items assigned and follow-up on May 22. We'll share patches, PromQL, dashboard JSON, SOC2/ISO.
09:35 Carlos Ruiz: Sounds good.
09:38 Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
09:40 Alex Kim: Thanks all — we'll send notes and the patch.
09:45 (call end)
